verdicts.details: ExtButtons.Extend(m) at ext.go:96 is unconditional, while the escape that keeps sanitized text from forming a button lives in the chain/markdown native, which on gnoland-1 equals the merge base at all four upgrades.json commits. Any gnoweb built from this head served against a node still on v1.5.0 turns user text passed through sanitize.Block (e.g. commondao renderBylaws, render.gno:441 at origin/chain/mainnet: res.Write(sanitize.Block(text))) into a live call-to-action styled as the realm's own. The window lasts until every RPC node gnoweb reads from carries the new native. Fix: gate ExtButtons behind a gnoweb option left off until the chain upgrade carrying the native ships, or ship the native first and state the order in the body.

verdicts.tldr: the rollout window of #3 again, plus a new diff-caused break: the inserted backslash kills a link destination and its bare brackets bind to the realm's own reference or footnote definitions
verdicts.details: The rollout half is the same window as #3 and rests on the same run. The distinct half: escapeGnoButtonTags (line 427) runs after escapeBracketsOutsideLinks (line 385), so for Block("[evil](<gno-button x>)") the walker spares the link, then `\<` breaks the angle destination and `[evil]` resolves against a realm reference definition the hosting page carries; `[^evil]` likewise binds a realm footnote. Output is also no longer idempotent: Block(Block(x)) differs. The cost is a user label rendered as the realm's own link or footnote, only where the realm defines a matching label. Fix: escape the button tag before the bracket walker, or have the walker treat `<gno-button` inside a destination as breaking the link so its brackets are escaped too.
